name: Yellowbone — The 2060s Reconstruction Aesthetic
description: Yellowbone devotees obsessively reconstruct the aesthetic and material culture of the 2060s — specifically the decade of the Great Consolidation, when corponations first achieved sovereign status and street culture responded with maximalist DIY fashion, early-generation visible chrome, and a specific palette of amber, ochre, and bone-white that defined the era's underground art. Practitioners are meticulous historians: they source or fabricate period-accurate first-gen augmentation shells (bulky, visible, utilitarian) and wear them over functional modern hardware as aesthetic overlays. The subculture is internally divided between 'Purists' who reject any post-2070 technology in their aesthetic and 'Layerists' who see anachronism as the point.
cultural_impact: Yellowbone has created a small but significant secondary market for authentic 2060s artifacts and early-gen chrome casings, driving up prices in salvage markets and occasionally bringing them into conflict with Shelf communities who need old-gen parts for actual functional repairs rather than aesthetics.
locations: The Depot — converted transit museum, Tier 3
Salvage Row flea markets, Shelf-Tier 2 border
story_hooks: A Yellowbone Purist acquires what appears to be an authentic 2063 corponation prototype augmentation shell — but it contains something that was never meant to be found, and the company it belonged to no longer officially exists.

Miroslav Tanaka-Osei's meticulous recreation of a 2060s underground art space is drawing crowds — and also the attention of an elderly woman who claims she actually lived there, and says he's gotten something dangerously wrong.

A Shelf salvager who's been selling 'authentic' 2060s chrome to Yellowbone collectors is exposed as a fabricator — but their fakes are so good that the Amber Archive wants to hire them, and someone else wants them silenced.
